goal: Evaluate pt-npwu0we6 (THFM-LoRA arm A, cl=81 single-seq overfit) in-train + OOT at the trained clip length, then diagnose why the in-train number is 47 mm despite training joint_l1 ≈ 5 mm/coord.

discoveries.title: ROOT CAUSE — train↔eval sampler divergence inflates the in-train joint_l2 number
discoveries.body: The headline 47.40 mm joint_l2 on the trained clip vs ~5.4 mm/coord training loss is a sampler bug, not a model defect. The `--encoder-mode thfm-lora --token-layout frame` trainer reaches `DexYCB16FrameClip._sample_frame_indices` (random-stride + random-pad-with-duplicates for span < clip_len), while the eval driver uses THFM pad-or-clip (`[ts..te, te*K]`). For a 63-frame sequence with cl=81, those produce different token→absolute-frame mappings; the per-frame hand head sees an OOD layout at eval. Memory note `feedback_thfm_81frame_paper_recipe.md` claimed this was fixed at 35b7330 — but that fix only covered `DexYCBGTCachedClip`, not the live loader used by arm A. See the in-page 'Diagnostic update' section for code citations and the verification numbers.

discoveries.title: Single-seq overfit converges in training but does not generalize
discoveries.body: Training loss total dropped from 1.58 to 0.0161 over 1990 steps on a single 63-tracked-frame clip replicated 64×. Eval at cl=81 on the same trained clip yields joint_l2=47.40 mm — the model has memorized the training window. On held-out same-subject sequences the mean rises to 132.75 mm; on OOT subject-07 to 162.26 mm. This single-sequence baseline confirms the THFM-LoRA pipeline trains end-to-end and reaches low loss; the next experiment is the full 50-seq subject-01-right manifest (per the spec) to test whether the same arch-and-loss recipe generalizes.

discoveries.title: Object rotation generalization breaks completely on OOT (24× error growth)
discoveries.body: Mean rot_err: train clip = 2.69°, in-dist held-out = 9.87°, OOT = 64.82°. The object-pose head (R6+t) has effectively memorised the near-identity rotation that fits the trained sequence's static-graspy interaction; on a held-out sequence with the same subject and similar objects the head is already off by 10° per frame, and on subject-07 with different objects it diverges to 65°. Translation degrades less aggressively (37 → 86 → 105 mm), so the bottleneck is rotational. This is the strongest argument for a multi-seq run before any anatomical-vs-frame layout comparison is meaningful — rotation needs more than one trajectory of supervision.

discoveries.title: Frame-layout cl=81 eval driver
discoveries.body: Existing p2_eval_thfm_lora.py raised NotImplementedError on --token-layout frame. Added p2_eval_thfm_lora_frame.py that mirrors the trainer's arm-A forward (QueryBank x2 + HandHead + ObjectHead + forward_with_queries + build_extras_coords) under torch.no_grad. Pad-or-clip emits one deterministic [ts..te, te, te, ...] window per sequence; VAECacheLoader.slice_clip already pads latents with the last frame.

Re-train pt-npwu0we6 with the patched loader to get a clean baseline; current published numbers (47/133/162 mm) are inflated by the sampler mismatch.

Verify whether pt-v9h8pfvl (arm D anatomical cl=81) is also hit by the same sampler bug. Anatomical uses extras tokens not frame tokens, but if the dataloader is shared the GT alignment still drifts. If yes, both arms need the fix.

caveats: ROOT-CAUSED: the headline 47/133/162 mm joint_l2 numbers are inflated by a train↔eval sampler mismatch (see 'Diagnostic update' section). True model quality on the trained clip drops to 11.88 mm when eval matches the trainer's _sample_frame_indices. Held-out and OOT numbers are similarly inflated and will need a post-fix re-eval.
Training used --max-manifest-size 1 --manifest-replicate 64, so the 'train set' is one 63-frame clip; the 49 other subject-01-right sequences in the manifest were never seen.
All sequences in subject-01 / subject-07 have 57–72 tracked frames, so every cl=81 clip is one padded window per sequence (last tracked frame repeated to length 81).
Frame-layout eval driver p2_eval_thfm_lora_frame.py is new in this session and now also carries `--use-train-sampler` for the diagnostic; neither is committed nor smoke-tested.
Hand-mesh metric is unavailable for arm A (HandHead returns 21 joints only); only joint_l2 / add_s / rot / trans are reported.
